PullRequest.Title: Engineering - run ESLint and hygiene only on changed files in batched CI builds
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request modifies the Azure DevOps product build pipeline to run ESLint and hygiene checks only on files that have changed in batched CI builds. 

### Changes made:
- **New Parameter**: Introduced `VSCODE_CHECK_CHANGED_FILES` in `product-build.yml` to control whether to limit checks to changed files.
- **New Step**: Added a "Hygiene & ESLint" step in `product-quality-checks.yml` that executes when the parameter is set, running both checks with the `--changed-since` option.
- **Commit Detection**: Implemented logic in `computeChangedSince.ts` to determine the base commit for the batch, ensuring accurate file change detection.
- **Validation**: Updated tests in `computeChangedSince.test.ts` to ensure the new functionality works as expected.

### Impact:
- Batched CI builds will now only check files that have changed, improving efficiency.
- Scheduled and manual builds remain unchanged, continuing to check all files. 

This change enhances the CI process by reducing unnecessary checks, aligning with the behavior of the GitHub PR checks.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The fallback control flow, full-scan behavior, task ordering, and before/after concurrency are explicit in the changed YAML and called scripts. Exact duration and failure frequency are uncertain, but the new API/fetch boundaries make the trigger realistic and the repository-wide work is known to be substantially larger than the intended changed-file path.
Findings.PerformanceResource: full-repository hygiene and ESLint CPU/filesystem work plus the compilation subprocesses that are delayed behind it
Findings.PerformanceScaling: When the new Azure changes request, shallow-history fetch, or base computation fails, VSCODE_CHANGED_SINCE remains unset and both checks scan the full repository; their entire runtime is then added before the six compilation checks can start, growing with repository size rather than the changed-file set.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased Quality-job wall-clock latency and a higher risk of hitting the existing 30-minute job timeout on transient scope-resolution failures
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The pre-PR command launched core-ci, full hygiene, full ESLint, and all five other compilation checks together under one npm-run-all2 invocation, so a successful job's critical path was approximately the slowest branch.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: This added command expands an unset VSCODE_CHANGED_SINCE to no arguments and performs full hygiene and ESLint in a separate task; the following Compile task cannot start until both full scans complete.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 165 invokes hygiene and eslint as a standalone pipeline step; added lines 167-170 place the compilation invocation in a subsequent step, while computeChangedSince.ts lines 96-99 deliberately convert every new network/git failure into a successful warning that leaves VSCODE_CHANGED_SINCE unset.
Findings.Title: Keep the full-check fallback concurrent with compilation
Findings.Impact: Any transient Azure DevOps API timeout/error, git fetch failure, or build with more than 1000 associated commits takes the fallback. In that case developers wait for full hygiene and ESLint to finish before compilation even begins, instead of those costs overlapping as they did before this PR.
Findings.Evidence: computeChangedSince performs a new Azure HTTP request with a 30-second timeout and a new git fetch, and its catch handler does not fail the task or set VSCODE_CHANGED_SINCE. The shell expansion on lines 164-165 therefore runs the unscoped package scripts. build/eslint.ts maps no arguments to the full eslintFilter, and build/gulpfile.hygiene.ts maps no changed-since value to hygiene(undefined, false). product-quality-checks.yml then starts Compile only after this step. The unchanged fallback before the PR was one parallel npm-run-all2 command.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the old combined npm-run-all2 invocation when VSCODE_CHANGED_SINCE is unset (for example, have scope resolution set a success variable and condition two task variants), while retaining the staged changed-file path only when a base was computed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Successful batched CI Quality job with a computable base commit
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After checkout, dependency setup, and other unchanged preparation, the new scope step must complete one Azure request and a shallow git-history fetch; changed-file hygiene and ESLint then complete together before the compilation checks start. This ordering adds the changed checks to the compilation critical path, but the diff explicitly bounds them to changed files and avoids memory overlap, so the net path is expected to improve versus full-repository checks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List up to 1000 commits associated with the Azure build
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One HTTP request per batched Quality job; continuation causes fallback rather than pagination
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Azure build-changes request occurred on this Quality-job path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks scope computation and therefore all hygiene, ESLint, and compilation checks for up to the 30-second timeout

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve HEAD, fetch depth commits+1 from origin, and enumerate first-parent history
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three serial git subprocesses per batched job, including one network fetch whose depth scales to at most 1001
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The depth-1 checkout was used directly and this extra history fetch did not occur.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All three block scope determination; the fetch downloads missing shallow history before checks can run

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run hygiene and ESLint, each invoking a local git diff for changed-file scope
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two check subprocesses in parallel and two independent git diff subprocesses over the same base-to-HEAD range
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same hygiene and ESLint checks ran full-repository concurrently with compilation; the git diff scope computations are newly introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before compilation starts; expected to take seconds for ordinary changed-file sets

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Lint and hygiene-check the effective changed-file scope
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Approximately one pass over each effective changed file, with ESLint extension-group/full-scope expansion for configured inputs
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both checks scanned the full repository on every product Quality job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before compilation, but normally replaces substantially larger full-repository scans

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run six compilation and build-check scripts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One npm-run-all invocation launching six parallel scripts
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These six scripts started concurrently with hygiene and ESLint in the same npm-run-all invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Begins only after changed hygiene and ESLint finish

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Azure build commit count, capped at 1000, determines fetch depth; the effective lint/hygiene cardinality is the deduplicated changed-file set, except configured global/type-aware inputs can expand it to the full repository or selected extension groups.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One Azure request and synchronous git subprocesses run serially in computeChangedSince; hygiene and ESLint run concurrently with each other; six compilation-related scripts run concurrently only afterward. Before the PR, hygiene, ESLint, and those six scripts all ran concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The agent checkout is depth 1, so every successful batched job performs the history fetch; no result cache or request coalescing is present. ESLint retains its existing content cache, while changed-file scope is recomputed independently by hygiene and ESLint via two local git diffs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: pipeline conditions, shallow checkout, boundary count, scope expansion, and task ordering are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact changed-file counts, fetch latency, ESLint cache hit rate, and memory-contention savings vary by batch; no timing data establishes the precise net reduction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the new API/fetch and serial stage are intentional overhead that unlocks much smaller checks, and the normal-path net performance is plausibly positive.

Scenarios.Scenario: Batched CI Quality job when changed-scope resolution fails or exceeds 1000 commits
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new Azure request or git operations fail, computeChangedSince logs a warning but exits successfully, then the standalone Hygiene & ESLint task runs both full-repository scans to completion before the Compile task can begin.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Attempt Azure build-change listing and shallow git history fetch
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One API attempt and, if it succeeds far enough, one git fetch attempt per job
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Neither failure-prone boundary was required before quality checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds up to 30 seconds plus fetch time before fallback checks

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan full repository with hygiene and ESLint
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two full-scope checks, independent of the batch's effective changed-file count
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full scans occurred, but overlapped the six compilation checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both must now finish before any compilation check starts

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run compilation/build checks after the full checks
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six parallel scripts after two full-check scripts
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Compilation started immediately alongside full hygiene and ESLint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The sequential stage boundary changes successful-job wall time from roughly max(full checks, compile checks) to full-check stage plus compile stage

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The fallback scans repository-wide hygiene and ESLint targets regardless of changed-file count; trigger cardinality includes transient API/fetch failures, a 30-second request timeout, missing environment/build metadata, unexpected build commit membership, shallow history not reaching a base, or more than 1000 associated commits.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Full hygiene and full ESLint run as two concurrent processes, followed by six concurrent compilation processes. Before the PR all eight processes overlapped, so the full-check duration is newly serialized ahead of compilation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no negative/error cache or alternate local base computation. Every affected job retries the new boundary path once and then performs full checks; ESLint's content cache may reduce CPU but does not restore overlap, and hygiene remains a repository-wide filesystem scan.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the catch handler leaves the variable unset, the shell explicitly omits --changed-since in that state, both check implementations select full scope, and Azure steps are sequential.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Failure frequency and exact full-check/compile durations are not measured, but the job has a fixed 30-minute timeout and the ordering penalty exists for every fallback.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported: the new fallback materially increases critical-path latency by serializing repository-wide checks before compilation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scheduled or manual product Quality build
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The template parameter evaluates false, so the unchanged combined Compile & Hygiene command remains on the critical path after preparation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the original eight quality scripts concurrently
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One npm-run-all invocation launching eight scripts

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Full repository check scope, as before the PR.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: core-ci, hygiene, ESLint, and five other checks run concurrently through one npm-run-all invocation, unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing dependency and ESLint caches remain unchanged; no new base-commit lookup or shallow-history fetch occurs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the compile-time template branch is directly controlled by Build.Reason through the new boolean parameter.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to diff causality; this path is intentionally unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: scheduled and manual builds preserve previous work, concurrency, and boundaries.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all five changed files and traced batched-success, batched-fallback, and scheduled/manual Quality-job paths. The intended changed-file path reduces lint/hygiene work; one reportable fallback regression remains because scope-resolution failures perform full checks in a new prerequisite stage rather than retaining the previous concurrency with compilation. No concrete shipped regression fix with blameable evidence was established.
